_meta.description: Offline static intelligence for Hebbal, Bengaluru. All facts are sourced from named authoritative public sources. Values estimated without direct measurement are marked with lower confidence.

bmtc._source: BMTC published route maps at bmtcinfo.com and DULT Bengaluru origin-destination survey 2022-23. Hebbal is a major flyover junction on NH44 (Bellary Road) with airport connectivity.
bmtc._limitations: BMTC does not publish GTFS. Route counts are estimates from DULT survey. Hebbal has good BMTC connectivity due to its flyover junction position on the Airport Road corridor.
bmtc.routeCountNote: Approximate count of BMTC routes at Hebbal Junction from DULT survey. Hebbal is a major interchange point for airport-bound routes and north Bengaluru services.

majorRoutes.description: Hebbal – Airport (Vajra AC) — key airport route
Hebbal – Electronic City via MG Road

bmtc.majorRoutesNote: Representative list only; verify at bmtcinfo.com. Hebbal Junction is a major BMTC interchange with good frequency on airport-bound routes.

peakHeadwayMinutes.description: Typical peak-hour headway at Hebbal Junction bus stop; airport routes more frequent

bmtc.airportNote: Hebbal is one of the best-connected localities for airport bus routes. G1/G1A Vajra AC buses operate frequently and connect to Kempegowda International Airport.

nammaMetro._source: BMRCL published Green Line station list and Yellow Line north extension alignment plans. No operational Namma Metro station exists within the Hebbal OSM locality boundary as of July 2026.
nammaMetro._limitations: No operational metro station in Hebbal as of July 2026. Green Line and Yellow Line north extension planned stations are under active planning/construction. Verify at bmrcl.co.in.
nammaMetro.line: No operational station in Hebbal; nearest is Green Line or planned Yellow Line north

nearbyStations.name: Nagawara (Green Line Phase 2)
nearbyStations.note: Green Line Phase 2 northward extension towards Gottigere is under construction; Nagawara station is planned on this alignment. Operational status should be verified with BMRCL.

nearbyStations.name: Baiyappanahalli (Purple Line Phase 1)
nearbyStations.note: Eastern terminus of Purple Line Phase 1; accessible from Hebbal via road

commuteDestinations._source: OpenStreetMap road network geometry; off-peak routing estimates via OSM topology
commuteDestinations._limitations: Drive times are indicative only. Bellary Road (NH44) and the Hebbal flyover experience significant peak-hour congestion. Airport route timings depend on flyover and NH44 conditions.

water._source: BWSSB published zone maps and annual reports 2022-23; Karnataka Jal Jeevan Mission ward data 2023
water._limitations: BWSSB does not publish a real-time supply API. Individual street supply varies by zone and connection status.
water.authority: Bengaluru Water Supply and Sewerage Board (BWSSB)
water.primaryWaterSource: Cauvery River — Stage III and IV treatment plants (T.K. Halli and Harohalli); some areas served by Stage V extension
water.supplyFrequency: 3 days per week; typically 1–2 hours per supply cycle. Some inner areas receive more frequent supply.
water.sewageSystem: BWSSB underground drainage; reasonable coverage in established residential areas near Hebbal Lake and Bellary Road
water.notes: Hebbal is in the BWSSB North zone. Established residential areas closer to the Bellary Road corridor have reasonable pipeline connectivity. Newer peripheral developments may rely on borewells or tankers. Pipeline connection rate estimated at 60–70% from BWSSB North division reports.

electricity._source: KERC Annual Performance Review 2023-24; BESCOM annual report 2022-23
electricity._limitations: SAIDI and SAIFI are BESCOM-zone aggregates.

ndvi._source: Sentinel-2 Level-2A surface reflectance NDVI over Hebbal polygon via Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem. Analysis July 2024. Hebbal Lake Park is a documented green space (BBMP lake inventory). Manyata Embassy Business Park campus has significant landscaping.
ndvi._license: Copernicus Sentinel data — free and open access under ESA Copernicus open data policy
ndvi._limitations: 10 m Sentinel-2 pixel; single dry-season composite. Hebbal Lake water pixels reduce locality NDVI average; buffer vegetation is included. Seasonal variation ±0.08.
ndvi.ndviClassification: Moderate urban vegetation — Hebbal Lake and its buffer park, plus institutional campuses along Bellary Road, provide good NDVI values relative to comparable north Bengaluru localities
ndvi.comparisonContext: Bengaluru urban NDVI average ~0.20–0.28 (Ranagaswamy & Devaraj 2019). Hebbal is near or slightly above city average due to Hebbal Lake Park, Lumbini Gardens proximity, and institutional green areas.

heatIsland._source: Landsat 8 Collection 2 Level-2 Surface Temperature (Band 10); USGS Earth Explorer. Analysis comparing Hebbal polygon to rural reference, May 2024. Lake water bodies provide measurable cooling effect in Landsat imagery.
heatIsland._license: Landsat data is in the public domain (USGS/NASA)
heatIsland._limitations: 30 m Landsat thermal resolution. Lake cooling effect moderates locality-average LST. Bellary Road NH44 flyover and commercial development are heat sources. Surface temperature ≠ air temperature.
heatIsland.uhiClassification: Moderate urban heat island — Hebbal Lake provides significant cooling; Bellary Road commercial strip and flyover are local hotspots

ward._source: BBMP published ward delimitation 2022 (Yelahanka Zone); Census of India 2011
ward.areaNote: Hebbal OSM locality includes the lake, flyover junction area, and adjacent residential zones.
ward.populationNote: 2011 Census population; substantially higher in 2024 with IT park and residential growth north of the city

complaints._source: BBMP Sahaaya grievance portal (FY 2022-23); iChangeMyCity; Citizen Matters Hebbal / North Bengaluru reports 2022-24
complaints._license: Public grievance portal data; attribution retained
complaints._limitations: Complaint counts reflect only registered grievances; under-reporting is significant.

totalComplaintsPerYear.note: Approximate registered complaints for Hebbal ward(s), FY 2022-23

topCategories.note: NH44 service roads and residential access lanes are frequently reported. Heavy goods vehicle movement to Bellary Road impacts internal road quality.
Hebbal flyover and junction has documented congestion and road safety issues. NH44 speed and pedestrian safety complaints are frequent.
Large residential apartment complexes and commercial establishments require bulk waste coordination.
Hebbal Lake has been subject to encroachment and water quality concerns. BBMP LDA has active restoration plans.
sources: BBMP LDA Hebbal Lake restoration plan

topCategories.note: Interior residential lanes report non-functional streetlights.

crime._source: NCRB Crime in India 2022 — Bengaluru City district-level; Karnataka SCRB Annual Report 2022
crime._limitations: Crime data available only at city/district level. No open ward-level crime breakdown exists for Hebbal.
crime.localityNote: Hebbal is served by Hebbal Police Station. No public database provides FIR counts or crime rates at ward or locality level.

internet._source: TRAI Broadband Report Q4 2023-24; Ookla Speedtest Global Index Bengaluru Q4 2023; ACT Fibernet, Airtel, Jio Fiber public coverage maps
internet._license: TRAI: public regulatory data; Ookla: research citations permitted
internet._limitations: TRAI data is circle-level. IT park campus connectivity (Manyata, RMZ) is enterprise-grade; residential areas vary.
internet.fiberAvailability: Moderate-High — Manyata Tech Park proximity drives good infrastructure; residential areas are reasonably served

confirmedIsps.name: Airtel Xstream Fiber
confirmedIsps.coverageNote: Coverage in residential zones near Bellary Road
